name: ainclave

plans.name: Design partner
plans.note: Unknown limits are not promises of unlimited capacity.

caveats: Design-partner access. Official pricing explicitly says rates are not yet published. Session wall-clock ready-to-stop, not CPU-active time. Shared and reserved dedicated bare-metal plans have different procurement but unpublished dollars.
On-prem and audit export are roadmap, not confirmed shipping features.
Not fully priceable in ENGINE_CARD: unknown USD resource rates or machine shape. Null is not zero; do not rank as a free provider.

Features set to null were not verified. No sandbox was purchased or tested; feature/performance statements are documentation claims. Null maximums are unknown unless a cited note explicitly states unlimited.
A complete monthly bill requires known snapshot/egress/plan limits; do not silently treat missing ancillary charges as free.

Billing meter is wall-clock from session 'ready' to stop. Idle time inside a running session is billed, bounded only by the optional user-set idle timeout. Budget caps are in runtime minutes (per session lifetime and per account per period) and stop the sessions (hard cap).

Status: pre-launch design-partner phase, operated by an individual (imprint: Hanna Novikova, Rauenberg, Germany). There is no DPA, no certification, no pen-test report, and no public CLI. Egress destinations are fixed by configuration (repo host, model endpoint, MCP endpoints); the self-service allowlist is roadmap.

fleet.notes: Pricing offers a design-partner/contact-led offering; no self-serve account resource quota or guaranteed fleet entitlement established.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: A self-service egress allowlist; export and tamper-evident anchoring for the session event feed; session persistence, resume and fork; a public CLI and agent skill; on-premises deployment; and an external penetration test report.
snapshot_auto.note: Listed under 'What is not built yet?'. Sessions stop on idle timeout / lifetime cap / account runtime budget; no state is saved (session persistence and resume are roadmap).

snapshot_on_demand.note: Under 'Roadmap — Designed and not shipped. None of the following is available today.' No snapshot/checkpoint/fork API today.

egress_allowlist.quote: Egress is deny-default: the baseline policy grants no destination at all. A session reaches only what its own configuration names at create time — the repository host, the model endpoint, configured MCP endpoints. That list is fixed for the life of the session. Enforcement sits on the host datapath, not in a proxy the workload could route around.
egress_allowlist.note: Host-enforced deny-default: host DNS resolver scoped to the session list + TLS forwarded only on exact hostname (SNI) match; cloud metadata unreachable. BUT the list is derived from the chosen configuration (repo host, model endpoint, MCP endpoints); a self-service, per-destination editable allowlist is roadmap.

secret_proxy.quote: It reaches the agent process only as a placeholder: the environment variable inside the guest carries a reference, and the real bearer token is substituted on the outbound request, so only the destination server sees it. The substitution happens outside the agent process, but the proxy that performs it terminates TLS inside the same guest, and nothing separates the two.
secret_proxy.note: Covers the BYOT model-provider token (and apparently source-control credentials: 'Provider and source-control credentials are stored as encrypted vault references'); users cannot register credentials for arbitrary hosts (destinations follow the config). Big caveat: the substituting proxy runs INSIDE the same microVM guest and terminates TLS there, so the real secret does enter the sandbox VM (just not the agent process); the vendor says whether the agent can reach it is untested. Non-HTTP protocols not covered/documented.

volume_attach.note: Listed under 'NOT BUILT YET'. Each session gets a repo mount (git remote cloned/mounted read/write); 'Volumes are encrypted' refers to backing storage, no attachable persistent volumes documented.

volume_shared.note: No persistent or shared volumes; one repo mount per session.
